questions.question: What selects the pull-up or pull-down of F14 on each of the 4 multiprotocol ports: a jumper per port, an RP2354B GPIO, an output of the I/O expander that drives the port switches, or a circuit with no control input that follows the port's signal?
questions.why: IOBoard.md:256 says what selects the bias is not stated, and R4 selects the part that sets it. P2 cannot choose the element or count its placements and control lines without the answer. The element could be a jumper, an analogue switch or MOSFET per port, or a buffer with its own pull.
questions.for_quantity: what selects the bias

questions.question: Does a bias selector driven by RP2354B firmware or by the I/O expander meet the rule that no processor, register or firmware sits in the path from GPIO6 to a gate (Monostable.md:449-455 at 23c82ca): yes or no? The selector is not in the enable path, but it sets the connector line's level while the gate is disabled.
questions.why: A selected pull-up holds a disabled line high. Pull request #167 makes low the disabled idle for servo pulses and DShot (Monostable.md:363-366). If the answer is no, the selector is a jumper or is driven from the enable node. P2 cannot qualify a firmware- or expander-driven selector until then.
questions.for_quantity: firmware or I/O expander selector under the Not defeatable rule
questions.asks: firmware or I/O expander selector under the GPIO6 path rule

questions.question: Which bias does each of these take, both with the gate disabled and with the pin released: the UART socket (OpenYGE, UART 8N1, idles high), and a multiprotocol port in ESC bootloader, ESC telemetry and servo configuration modes, whose lines idle high? For each, the choices are a pull-up (value in kΩ, to which rail in V), the 10 kΩ pull-down that F14's 'otherwise' reads as, or no bias of the board's own.
questions.why: F14 gives a pull-down to every protocol except bidirectional DShot, and a 10 kΩ pull-down sits against the pull-up that holds these lines high (IOBoard.md:280). The AM32 bootloader jumps to its application when the line is not high within 20 ms (AM32-bootloader bootloader/main.c:840-852, read 2026-09-28T10:30:23Z). ESCape32 enters its CLI only with the line held high for 2 s at startup (ESCape32 wiki Configuration, read 2026-09-28T10:29:53Z). P2 cannot size or select the bias element per mode without the answer.
questions.for_quantity: bias of the UART socket and the modes whose lines idle high
questions.asks: bias of the UART socket and the modes whose lines idle high

questions.question: At what baud rate does the ESCape32 text CLI run on a multiprotocol port? The tree's only figure is 19,200 baud, in the proposed analyser map (testbench/README.md:396). ESCape32's wiki (https://github.com/neoxic/ESCape32/wiki/Configuration, read 2026-09-28T10:29:53Z) gives 38,400 baud 8N1 on the signal line.
questions.why: P2 checks the multiprotocol path and the rise time of its bias network against the highest serial rate a port carries. The tree's figure is a proposal, and the primary source gives a different rate.
questions.for_quantity: ESCape32 baud

questions.question: What signal levels does the Hitec D-series protocol use on the servo's signal wire: the high level the servo drives, and the input-high threshold it needs, in V?
questions.why: The tree names the published protocol (docs/Manifest.md:32; shared/ui/programmer_screen.c:246-247, Hitec D956TW) and gives no levels (IOBoard.md:265). P2 cannot check the path's connector-side level and thresholds for servo configuration mode without them.
questions.for_quantity: Hitec D-series levels

questions.question: What is the Hitec D-series protocol's electrical form on the port: one signal wire at half duplex or separate lines, UART normal or inverted, and the servo's output stage (push-pull, or open drain with a pull-up at its own supply)?
questions.why: IOBoard.md:265 says the form is not stated. It decides whether the multiprotocol path has to pass both directions on one line for servo configuration mode, and which bias that mode needs.
questions.for_quantity: Hitec D-series electrical form

questions.question: At what baud rate does the Hitec D-series protocol run, in baud?
questions.why: IOBoard.md:265 says the rate is not stated. P2 checks the path and its bias network against the highest rate a multiprotocol port carries.
questions.for_quantity: Hitec D-series baud

questions.question: What high level must each port's signal line drive at the connector, in V: 3.3 V, 5 V, or the level of a supply sensed from the device, and then which rail? It applies to the 16 PWM ports, the 4 multiprotocol ports and the UART socket.
questions.why: IOBoard.md:255 gives 'commonly 5 V' from a bench guide, and a translator that senses 'the target's rail' without naming the rail. A servo port's supply pin carries up to 8.4 V, with an 8.7 V ceiling (F16). A logic test point may carry 5 V at most (IOBoard.md:539). P2 cannot choose between a 3.3 V buffer, a 3.3 V to 5 V translator and an auto-sensing translator, or set the connector-side supply, without the answer.
questions.for_quantity: connector-side signal level

questions.question: What is the value of the pull-up F14 puts on a line that carries bidirectional DShot, in kΩ, and to which rail, in V?
questions.why: IOBoard.md:256 says the pull-up's value is not stated. It sets the idle level at the ESC, the rise time of the reply's rising edges at 750 kbit/s (the DShot600 reply) and the current the buffer sinks while driving low. P2 cannot qualify the bias element or check the buffer's drive against it without the value.
questions.for_quantity: bidirectional DShot pull-up value and rail

questions.question: What is the highest DShot bit rate the gated output path must pass, in kbit/s: 600, the bench's bind list (shared/outputs/out_bind.c:566-569), or 1200, the driver's range (shared/outputs/outputs.c:29)?
questions.why: IOBoard.md:282 says the rate the output path is specified for is not stated. P2 checks each buffer's data rate and propagation-delay skew against the bit. At 600 kbit/s the bit is 1.67 µs with a 0.63 µs zero-bit high. At 1200 kbit/s it is 0.83 µs with a 0.31 µs zero-bit high.
questions.for_quantity: highest DShot bit rate on the gated path

questions.question: What load must each output drive at that bit rate: the longest lead from the connector to the servo or ESC, in m, or the load capacitance, in pF?
questions.why: Neither page states a lead length or load. A buffer's data rate and edge times, and the rise time of a pull-up bias, are specified at a stated load capacitance. P2 cannot confirm the rate at the connector without it.
questions.for_quantity: load on an output at the DShot bit rate

questions.question: Which wire does VESC's 115,200-baud framed-packet link use on the IO board, and how many signal lines does it take: one half-duplex line on a multiprotocol port, the UART socket, or separate transmit and receive lines (2)?
questions.why: IOBoard.md:286 says the wire and line count are not stated. An output lead has 3 wires: signal, ground and rail (IOBoard.md:531). P2 cannot count the lines and directions the multiprotocol path carries without the answer.

questions.question: How many receiver inputs does the IO board bring out (a count)?
questions.why: IOBoard.md:61 and :287 say the count is not stated. P2 needs the placements per board for sourcing rule 4 and the channel count of any input buffer.

questions.question: What is the highest voltage a receiver drives on its signal wire into the IO board, in V?

GPIO0 to 39 take 5.5 V only while IOVDD is at 3.3 V and 3.63 V while it is at 0 V, and GPIO40 to 47 take IOVDD + 0.5 V (RP2350 datasheet build 2025-07-29, Table 1433, read 2026-09-28T10:25:13Z). P2 cannot decide whether an input needs translation or a series resistor, or which part, without it.
questions.for_quantity: receiver signal level

questions.question: What is the highest baud rate of any receiver bus on a receiver input, in baud? The buses are iBUS, SUMD, CRSF, SRXL2 and JETI EX Bus; S.BUS is 100 kbaud.
questions.why: IOBoard.md:287 says the baud of iBUS, SUMD, CRSF, SRXL2 and JETI EX Bus is not stated. P2 checks any input buffer or filter against the highest rate.
questions.for_quantity: highest receiver bus baud

questions.question: Does the bench transmit on a receiver input, for JETI EX Bus telemetry (docs/Manifest.md:37-39) or SRXL2: yes or no, for each bus?
questions.why: IOBoard.md:287 says it is not stated. A transmit direction makes the receiver input a bidirectional path with its own idle level and bias. P2 cannot choose between a one-way input buffer and a bidirectional part without the answer.

questions.question: Does a receiver input pass the output gate of F13: yes or no? F13's answer names only the 20 output ports and the UART socket.
questions.why: IOBoard.md:279 lists it as not known. If yes, the receiver path takes the gate's enable, I_off and bias requirements, and P2 qualifies it as part of the gated buffer.
questions.for_quantity: receiver inputs through the output gate

questions.question: The gate stays enabled while the RP2354B is held in reset or restarts through the watchdog, because the enable follows the monostable (owner, 2026-09-25). During that time, which level must these lines hold at the connector: a multiprotocol port bound to a mode whose line idles high (bidirectional DShot, ESC telemetry, servo configuration, ESC bootloader), and the UART socket? Is it that mode's idle, high, or low?
questions.why: The RP2350's pads reset with a pull-down and the output disabled (datasheet build 2025-07-29, section 9.3 and Table 1427, read 2026-09-28T10:25:13Z). The I/O expander resets with the RP2354B (IOBoard.md:340). A bias selected in firmware or on the expander is therefore lost in the reset. The R4 row requires every connector output at 'its idle level' in reset but states no level for these modes. P2 cannot tell whether the bias element must hold its state through a reset without the answer.
questions.for_quantity: connector idle level in reset for modes whose lines idle high

questions.question: Must the connector side of a bidirectional line also carry I_off or a series resistor of 4.7 kΩ or more: yes or no? The lines are the 4 multiprotocol ports, the UART socket and a receiver input. The case is a device on its own supply, such as an ESC's BEC or a receiver on another supply, driving the line while the IO board is unpowered.
questions.why: Pull request #167's isolation rule names only the buffer's RP2350-side inputs and its enable (Monostable.md:88). In the reply direction the connector side is an input driven from outside. P2 cannot pass or fail a translator on connector-side I_off without the answer.
questions.for_quantity: connector-side isolation of bidirectional ports and receiver inputs

questions.question: Which faults on a connector signal line must the buffer survive, and for how long, in s or continuous: a short to ground, and a short to the port's supply pin at up to 8.7 V (the HV ceiling of F16)?
questions.why: IOBoard.md:536 says no requirement in the tree limits the current into a shorted signal line at an output connector. P2 cannot size the series resistance, choose a clamp, or check the buffer's output-current and overvoltage ratings without the answer.
questions.for_quantity: fault a connector signal line survives

questions.question: Besides OpenYGE ESCs, which serial devices does the UART socket carry, and what is the highest baud rate among them, in baud?
questions.why: IOBoard.md:65 names 'other serial devices' with no protocol, rate or level. OpenYGE is 115,200 baud 8N1 (docs/OpenYGE.md:21). P2 checks the socket's path and bias against the highest rate it carries.
questions.for_quantity: UART socket devices and highest baud
